description:
Report server version and whether the Godot editor bridge is connected.

Use this first to confirm the server is up and that Godot is reachable
before issuing other commands. Also reports the connected addon's version
and flags a server↔addon version mismatch. Never mutates anything.
name: godot_health_check

outputSchema.description: Server status and Godot bridge connection state.

title: Godot Health Check

description:
Undo the last ``count`` editor actions on the current scene's history.

With ``dry_run=True``, previews (``has_undo`` + ``would_undo_next``) without
undoing. Otherwise returns ``{undone, requested, last_action,
nothing_to_undo}``. Undoing an empty history is a no-op (``undone == 0``,
``nothing_to_undo == True``), not an error — the reversibility ledger decides
what that means.

No node/scene target to precondition — ``route()`` already surfaces a
disconnected bridge as a structured ``BRIDGE_DISCONNECTED`` error.
name: godot_undo
title: Godot Undo

description:
Redo the last ``count`` undone editor actions on the current scene's history.

The mirror of ``godot_undo``: with ``dry_run=True``, previews (``has_redo`` +
``would_redo_next``) without redoing; otherwise returns ``{redone, requested,
last_action, nothing_to_redo}``. Redoing with nothing to redo is a no-op
(``redone == 0``, ``nothing_to_redo == True``), not an error. Use
``godot_list_history`` first when unsure which direction is available.
name: godot_redo
title: Godot Redo

description:
Inspect the current scene's editor undo history before mutating.

Returns the version counter (increments on every committed action — a
cheap change-detector), ``has_undo`` / ``has_redo`` availability, the
current action name, the history depth, and the most recent action
names (capped, most recent last). Empty history returns zero-values,
not an error. Use it to orient before ``godot_undo`` / ``godot_redo``.
name: godot_list_history

items.description: One editor undo-history action, named for agent orientation.

outputSchema.description:
``godot_list_history`` response: the editor history's orientation data.

``version`` increments on every committed action — a cheap change-detector
the agent can compare across calls. ``depth`` counts the history entries
(``get_history_count``, 4.4+); ``recent`` names up to 20 entries, most
recent last (``get_action_name`` indices are 0-based over the history).
``can_redo`` is the #529 ticket's field name — a documented alias of
``has_redo``, emitted so the envelope matches the issue's field list.

title: Godot List History

description:
Describe an engine class's ClassDB metadata: settable properties
(with defaults and types), methods (typed args + return), signals,
integer constants, enums, the inheritance chain, and instantiability.

Use BEFORE setting properties or calling methods by trial-and-error:
the ``type`` fields are Variant.Type names — exactly the shapes the
coercion layer accepts for ``set_node_property`` values. Engine classes
only (script ``class_name`` globals are not in ClassDB; an unknown name
returns VALIDATION_ERROR with did-you-mean suggestions). Default flags
list the class's OWN members; ``include_inherited=True`` widens every
list to the full ancestry; ``include_private=True`` keeps
``_``-prefixed entries.
name: godot_describe_class
title: Godot Describe Class

description:
Get project-level context: name, Godot version, main scene, autoloads,
and project-defined input actions. Call this to orient before editing.
name: godot_inspection_get_project_info
title: Godot Inspection Get Project Info

description:
Get the currently open scene's path and name. Returns ``is_open=False``
when no scene is open (not an error).
name: godot_inspection_get_active_scene

outputSchema.description: The currently open scene, or ``is_open=False`` when none is open.

title: Godot Inspection Get Active Scene

description:
List the project's scene files (``res://*.tscn``) and their editor state —
which is the ``main_scene``, which are open, and which is active.

Call this to decide, when no scene is open, whether to OPEN an existing scene
(a modification / enhancement / bugfix of something already there) or CREATE a
net-new one:
  - no scenes at all -> the project is empty; godot_scene_edit_create_scene(
    root_type=…, scene_path=…) to start one (enable the scene_edit toolset first).
  - exactly one scene -> godot_scene_edit_open_scene(scene_path=that path).
  - several scenes -> open the one the request targets, or ask which to use.
Returns an empty ``scenes`` list for a project with no scenes yet (not an error).
name: godot_inspection_list_scenes

items.description: One project scene file and its editor state (#304).

outputSchema.description:
The project's scene files + which is main, for open-vs-create decisions (#304).

``scenes`` is empty for a project with no scenes yet (a net-new signal, not an error).

title: Godot Inspection List Scenes

description:
Get the open scene as a recursive tree of {name, type, path, script, children}.

Each node carries a scene-relative ``path`` (root ".") — pass it verbatim to
set_node_property / create_node(parent_path) / attach_script; never rebuild it
by hand. ``max_depth`` bounds child levels (-1 unlimited, 0 root only); a tree
over the output limit returns lightweight with ``truncated=true``. ``tree`` is
null when no scene is open. For the *running* game use get_game_scene_tree().
See docs/tool-contracts.md for ``lightweight``.
name: godot_inspection_get_scene_tree

outputSchema.description: The active scene tree, or ``tree=None`` when no scene is open.

title: Godot Inspection Get Scene Tree

description:
Get the node currently selected in the editor — its path, type, script,
properties, and child names. Returns ``selected=None`` when nothing is
selected.
name: godot_inspection_get_selected_node

anyOf.description: Full detail for a single node (path, type, script, properties, children).

outputSchema.description: The selected node, or ``selected=None`` when nothing is selected.

title: Godot Inspection Get Selected Node

description:
Get a node's detail by scene-relative path (e.g. "Player/Sprite2D"):
type, attached script, exported/set properties, and child names. Errors
with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if the path doesn't resolve, or PRECONDITION_FAILED
if no scene is open.
name: godot_inspection_get_node_properties

outputSchema.description: Full detail for a single node (path, type, script, properties, children).

title: Godot Inspection Get Node Properties

description:
Read a single ``property`` by name from the node at ``node_path`` — including
**built-in** Godot properties (position, scale, modulate, collision_layer,
material, theme, …) that ``get_node_properties`` omits (it returns only
script-declared variables). Returns ``{value, exists}``; ``exists=false``
(value null) when the node has no such property. The value is JSON-coerced
(Vector2 as {"x","y"}, Color, NodePath as string). Use it to snapshot a value
before ``set_node_property`` — for verification or rollback. Errors with
RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if the path doesn't resolve, or PRECONDITION_FAILED if no
scene is open.
name: godot_inspection_get_node_property

outputSchema.description:
A single node property read (issue #215), including built-in Godot properties.

``value`` is JSON-coerced (see type_coerce.gd); ``exists`` is false (and ``value``
null) when the node has no such property.

title: Godot Inspection Get Node Property

description:
Return the flat list of valid property names for the node at
``node_path``, plus its runtime class name. Use this to discover what
properties you can set before calling ``set_node_property``.
name: godot_inspection_get_node_property_list

outputSchema.description: All property names for a node, returned by get_node_property_list.

title: Godot Inspection Get Node Property List

description:
List the groups the node at ``node_path`` belongs to (``{groups: [name]}``),
excluding editor-internal groups (names beginning with "_"). Use it to snapshot
membership before ``add_to_group`` / ``remove_from_group`` (or a delete) so the
change is reversible. Errors with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if the path doesn't resolve,
or PRECONDITION_FAILED if no scene is open.
name: godot_inspection_get_node_groups

outputSchema.description:
A node's group memberships (issue #216), editor-internal groups excluded.

Inverts ``add_to_group`` / ``remove_from_group`` and lets
``godot_scene_edit_delete_node`` restore
membership.

title: Godot Inspection Get Node Groups

description:
Snapshot a subtree as a stable dict (issue #535): node paths, types, script
paths, and per-node property values. Captured by default: script vars,
transforms (position/rotation/scale where the class exposes them), and group
memberships — so transform/group changes show in a diff without naming them.
``properties`` adds further built-ins by name. Returns a ``snapshot_id`` that
references the server-side store — pass it to ``diff_snapshots`` to verify a
batch mutation in one round-trip (mutate → diff → assert) instead of N
re-reads. ``max_depth`` caps depth (-1 = unlimited), like ``get_scene_tree``.
Errors with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if the path doesn't resolve, or
PRECONDITION_FAILED if no scene is open.
name: godot_inspection_snapshot_subtree

outputSchema.description:
A subtree snapshot (issue #535): a stable id + the serialized subtree.

``snapshot_id`` references the server-side bounded store — pass it to
``diff_snapshots`` (as ``before_id``/``after_id``) instead of re-serializing.

title: Godot Inspection Snapshot Subtree

description:
Diff two subtree snapshots taken with ``snapshot_subtree`` (issue #535):
``{added: [node], removed: [node], changed: [{node, property, before, after}]}``.
All three lists empty means identical. With ``after_id`` unset, the tool
re-reads the same ``node_path`` live and diffs snapshot-vs-now — the natural
acceptance check after ``batch_set_property`` / ``apply_node_edits`` /
``run_commands``. Errors with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND for an unknown/evicted id
(re-snapshot, the store is bounded).
name: godot_inspection_diff_snapshots

items.description: One property-level difference between two snapshots (issue #535).

outputSchema.description:
The diff of two subtree snapshots (issue #535).

``added``/``removed`` list node paths; ``changed`` lists per-property
before/after pairs (JSON-coerced shapes). All three empty = identical.

title: Godot Inspection Diff Snapshots

description:
Read a godot:// context resource by URI — the fallback for MCP clients
without resource-protocol support. Known URIs: godot://project/info,
godot://scene/current, godot://scene/tree, godot://scene/tree/{max_depth},
godot://node/selected.
name: godot_read_resource
title: Godot Read Resource

description:
Run a comprehensive debug check on the project and return a unified report.

This aggregates multiple diagnostics into one call so you (or the LLM) can
spot problems quickly without calling each tool individually.

Checks performed:
1. Parse errors across all GDScript files
2. Active scene tree structure (nodes, scripts, properties)
3. Headless run of the project (or a specific scene) capturing errors/warnings
4. Bridge connection state and Godot version

``scene`` — optional res:// path to focus the headless run on a specific scene.
``expected_timeout`` — set true when the game legitimately runs until killed
(sandbox/live-service games with no quit path): a timeout then means the run
behaved as designed and is not reported as a finding.
name: godot_debug_workflow
title: Godot Debug Workflow

description:
List every available tool grouped by its safety class
(read_only / mutating / destructive / runtime). Call this to learn which
tools are safe to call freely and which need ``dry_run``/``confirm``.
name: godot_list_tools_by_safety_class

tools_by_safety_class.description: Tool names keyed by safety_class (read_only / mutating / destructive / runtime); unclassified tools (if any) appear under 'unclassified'.

outputSchema.description: Result of ``list_tools_by_safety_class`` — tool names grouped by safety class.

title: Godot List Tools By Safety Class

description:
List the available toolsets (tool categories) and whether each is currently
enabled. Enable a toolset with enable_toolset before using its tools.
name: godot_list_toolsets

items.description: One exposed tool's identity + input schema (issue #621).

title: Godot List Toolsets

description:
Expose a toolset's tools for this session. ``category`` is a toolset name
(e.g. "scene_edit"), a **bundle** — ``author`` (build scenes/scripts/assets),
``playtest`` (run/drive/observe the game), ``ship`` (export) — or a
comma-separated list of either (issue #653). A bundle/list enables all its
members in ONE call and returns a combined result whose ``tools`` carries
every enabled member tool's schema. Does not change the Godot project.
name: godot_enable_toolset

items.description: One exposed tool's identity + input schema (issue #621).

title: Godot Enable Toolset

description:
Hide a toolset's tools again to keep the active tool surface small. Accepts
a toolset name, a bundle, or a comma-separated list of either (issue #653).
name: godot_disable_toolset

items.description: One exposed tool's identity + input schema (issue #621).

title: Godot Disable Toolset

description:
Check whether a newer godot-mcp release is available.

Opt-in and offline by default: with ``GODOT_MCP_CHECK_UPDATES`` unset the
result reports ``enabled: false`` and makes no network request. When enabled
it queries the release feed and reports ``{current, latest, update_available,
url}``; an unreachable feed returns an ``error``/``hint`` rather than failing.
Read-only — never touches the Godot project.
name: godot_check_for_updates

outputSchema.description: The result of an update check — always a value, never a raised error.

title: Godot Check For Updates

description:
Return a comprehensive snapshot of the server's capabilities, toolsets,
prompts, bridge state, and common troubleshooting scenarios.

Use this at the **start of every session** to orient the agent:
it tells you which toolsets are available, how many tools each has,
whether Godot is connected, what scene is open, and what to do next.
name: godot_get_server_info

items.description: Summary of one toolset for the diagnostics report.

anyOf.description: Scripting backend capability of the connected editor/project (issue #207).
The result of an update check — always a value, never a raised error.

outputSchema.description:
Complete server capability and health snapshot.

This is the authoritative response to ``get_server_info`` — it tells the
client everything about what is available, what is enabled, and how to fix
common problems.

title: Godot Get Server Info
